title: Multiple-positive aggregate contrastive loss
formal_object: Released positive set P subset of allowed labeled candidate set A; scores s_j=q^T M c_j; T>0; positive-only and allowed softmax distributions.
assumptions: Every positive is released/known; unknown relevance is not a negative label.
A has at least one valid positive; a nontrivial new comparison needs genuine multiple positives.
Candidate identities and labels stay unchanged in the native test scorer.

operations.condition: Both finite partition sums are nonempty
operations.output: Differentiate to obtain allowed mass minus positive-conditioned mass.

operations.input: Claim that all known positives are equally pulled
operations.condition: More than one unequal positive logit
operations.output: The aggregate inside-log loss can favor an easy positive instead of equally supervising every positive.

derivation_steps.justification: Derivative of each log partition under the same fixed labels.

derivation_steps.statement: If |P|=1 the loss reduces to the same single-positive softmax objective.
derivation_steps.justification: The positive log partition becomes s_pos/T.

derivation_steps.statement: Outside-log supervision has dL_out/ds_j=(p_A(j)-1{j in P}/|P|)/T.
derivation_steps.justification: Averaging log probabilities yields uniform target mass; it differs from p_P for unequal positive scores. The inside-log objective already appears in SupCon Eq.3, up to a label-count constant.

method_expression: Fit bilinear M with the aggregate positive log partition on only released allowed candidates; block absent real multi-positive supervision.
distinguishing_prediction: The aggregate loss weights each positive in proportion to its current positive-only softmax; easy positives can dominate, unlike uniform-target SupCon.
falsifier: No released multi-positive rows collapses the distinction. Uniform-target SupCon performing as well or better at identical information/cost defeats the proposed necessity.
closest_alternative: SupCon inside-log Eq.3 is a direct objective match; author SupConLoss.forward implements outside-log Eq.2. A single-positive control alone is inadequate.
decisive_comparison: On unchanged native tasks compare aggregate, outside-log and single-positive while giving each arm the same known label information; C_SINGLE masks other positive targets but keeps them in allowed, so it also changes the treatment of known positives.
legacy_code_audit: Legacy fit(I05) gradient matches aggregate loss. Multi-positive guard checks the selected actual rows. No full multi-positive acquisition/merge proof or matched outside-log control exists.
review_limit: Conditional derivative reviewed; direct known-objective overlap retained, novelty adjudication pending.
